title: Segregation on tour in the South
summary: A white road manager got food for the band in some places.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Another thing too, that some times you look back on it. And, there have been so many strides, social strides, I mean. You know, in terms of black and white, and, you know. And in a band such as yours, and travelling over, as you said, all of the states

Oh, yeah. We had some of that. Only, only places I can remember is we hit some spots in the South. You know. And, the only thing we did, we (inaudible) like we had the road manager which was white. And, instead of us going out to go and get certain foods and things, he'd go in and get it for us just to keep down trouble cause there wasn't no interest for the colored at that time, or black, you know.

So, we'd do that so we could move on. You know? Then, we'd go to another spot where the things would be just opposite. We'd go in and get it ourselves. You know, we may not be able to sit down, but we could go in and order what we'd want and bring it out. But, we had that, you know, in some parts of the South. Then, I understood it. I
was born in Birmingham. But, I knew about it. But it's like I said, I never had to go through too much to not to know what to do, to get excited or be bothered.

In Birmingham, I had white friends and black friends. You know like it is. I knew what I, what not to do at that time cause I was young, you know, and I didn't want to handle trouble. I didn't care for trouble, you know.
